claim: Stated confidence from fine-tuned or well-prompted models can be calibrated on closed tasks: Kadavath (52B, lettered options), Lin (verbalized probability beats zero-shot logit under shift on Multi-answer, MSE 22.0 vs 37.4).
agent_test: Compare stated confidence to accuracy on closed-form items, equal tokens, ECE and Brier

claim: Off-the-shelf verbalized confidence from RLHF chat models beats token probabilities on ECE (gpt-3.5 TriviaQA 0.068 vs 0.140; SciQ top-4 0.065 vs 0.256; TruthfulQA top-4 0.203 vs 0.451) but top-1 gains are smaller (SciQ 0.234).
agent_test: Elicit top-k alternatives then confidence in one call; compare ECE with logit-free baseline

claim: Low ECE does not mean useful discrimination: GPT-4 on GSM8K scores ECE 0.064 by saying 100% for everything (93.6% accuracy); vanilla verbalized AUROC for GPT-4 averages 62.7%, near chance.
agent_test: Always report AUROC and a constant-confidence baseline next to ECE

claim: Sampling consistency (about 5 samples) raises failure-prediction AUROC far above single verbalized confidence (GSM8K GPT-4 54.8 to 92.7), at linear token cost. [Gap search: also Ghosh 2026, 10-sample agreement has 2x resolution of verbal confidence in 0.5-7B models; Boubnovski 2026, a trace-based K=4 score beats SC@8, AUC 0.78 vs 0.71, on Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 4.6.]
schema_part: O (sample then aggregate); links to ensembles subfield
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare 5 samples + agreement vs 1 sample + stated confidence vs best-of-5

claim: Verbalized confidence saturates: small instruction-tuned models put 95%+ on about 92% of numeric answers; confidence barely tracks token log-prob. [Gap search: saturation confirmed in open 0.5-8B and reasoning models (under 5% of responses below 0.5; 13,121 of 15,000 at 90+), but 15 frontier models in ConfidenceBench reach Brier 0.103 and use low values, so it is a small-model problem, not proven for frontier.]
agent_test: Measure the share of answers at 95%+ and spread of stated values on our model; use discrete bins

claim: Models rarely hedge and hedges are not tied to correctness: strengtheners in 20% vs weakeners 14%; 47% error in certainty-marked answers; faithfulness cMFG about 0.5 for vanilla prompts, at most 0.63 to 0.70 with prompting.
agent_test: Score hedge words against correctness on held-out questions

claim: Humans over-trust confident wording: users relied on 81% of strengtheners when 66% were correct; explanation length raises human confidence without raising discrimination (AUC 0.54 long vs model 0.75-0.78 vs human 0.59).
agent_test: Constrain the final message wording to match calibrated confidence; test with a reader model

claim: Training can fix verbal confidence: RLCR cuts ECE 0.37 to 0.03 in-domain at equal accuracy (61.7 vs 63.0); calibration-reward PPO and fine-tuning on about 1000 graded examples help; plain binary RL hurts calibration. A prompt scaffold cannot reproduce this. [Gap search: a training-free scored-feedback prompt (REHEARSE) cuts average ECE 58% but does not lead on AUROC; RL reward schemes can be hacked.]
schema_part: none (training; out of scope for scaffold)
agent_test: Not testable without training; use as upper bound

claim: Reasoning models express confidence better than non-reasoning counterparts (strictly better in 33 of 36 settings), but effects depend on task difficulty and long chains can raise ECE in small models. [Gap search: reasoning effort helps Brier in GPT-5 (0.141 Low vs 0.117 Standard) but reasoning in the same prompt as the confidence report disrupts the confidence direction in open models.]
agent_test: Ask confidence after reasoning vs before at equal tokens, on easy and hard sets

claim: Agent decisions do not follow stated confidence: models almost never abstain even when abstaining is optimal, penalties up to 100 do not change behaviour. [Gap search: verbal confidence predicts the model own abstain choice better than correctness (median AUROC gap +0.16).]
agent_test: Add an explicit abstain threshold in the scaffold and measure utility under penalties

claim: In agents, confidence is a usable control signal if outcome-grounded: AUQ +10.7 to +13.6 success; BrowseConf threshold test-time scaling; trained step confidence AUROC 0.68-0.85. But 90-94% bin had only 53% accuracy.
agent_test: Trigger re-verification when stated confidence < threshold; compare against fixed extra pass

claim: Human verbal probability phrases are vague and variable across people (Kent 1964 scale; Wallsten 1986 individual membership functions; SD 11-17 points), so a word-to-number map must be fixed per agent.
agent_test: Fix a 5-bin vocabulary with numeric anchors and check bin accuracy

claim: Human overconfidence classics: 20% wrong at full certainty; 90% intervals hit as low as 50%; more information raised confidence 33 to 53% with accuracy flat.
agent_test: Interval-forecast test on our agent

claim: Mechanism: verbal confidence is computed at the answer-adjacent cached position, not read from log-probs (log-probs explain 10% of variance vs 38% for activations), and is inflated by a small circuit.
agent_test: Not testable in a scaffold

claim: Temperature scaling (T=2.5) largely repairs RLHF calibration curves on MMLU/TruthfulQA in Kadavath; ECE of RLHF models is higher.
agent_test: Check whether sampling temperature changes stated-confidence ECE

claim: Frontier-model stated-confidence AUROC on knowledge benchmarks is only fair, 0.58 to 0.79 across six model-benchmark settings (3 of 6 above 0.7), and no paper found measures it on later-resolving forecasting questions.
agent_test: Measure AUROC of stated confidence on ForecastBench-like questions that resolve later, with a constant-confidence baseline

claim: Frontier reasoners are not saturated: ConfidenceBench Brier 0.103 for Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro vs 0.1875 for calibrated-random, but model spread is wide (0.367 for Flash-Lite) and unknowable items sit on a 25% floor.
agent_test: Count how often each bin is used; flag if over 80% of answers fall in one bin

claim: Confidence rated in a separate blind pass after the answer beats confidence stated in the same pass: ECE gains 17-88% in Gemma-3 (shrinking with size), and same-prompt reasoning contaminates the confidence direction in open 7B models. Not tested on frontier models.
agent_test: A/B: confidence in the same call vs separate blind rating call, compare AUROC and ECE

claim: Prompt-only calibration exists but is weaker than training: REHEARSE cuts ECE 58% on average, Twin-Pass up to 88%, but neither shows an AUROC gain comparable to RLCR (ECE 0.37 to 0.03).
agent_test: Test a scored-feedback prefix; report AUROC, not only ECE

claim: Calibration does not transfer freely across tasks: plain fine-tuned confidence degrades out-of-distribution (SFT ECE 0.61 to 0.625); critique training gives only small gains (ECE 0.571); verbalized formats on the same model correlate poorly (Spearman -0.07 to +0.25).
agent_test: Re-measure calibration per task type; never reuse a bin map across types

claim: Original human-overconfidence numbers (Lichtenstein 1982, Wallsten 1986) remain unverified in this pass; Moore and Healy 2008 abstract confirms the hard-easy reversal of overestimation and that overprecision is the most persistent form.
agent_test: Do not cite the classic numbers from this file as checked; read the DTIC reports first

claim: Plain ECE can mislead: verbal confidence matches the best ECE (0.0356) while sampling agreement has twice the resolution; and verbal confidence tracks the model own commit decision more than correctness (AUROC gap +0.16).
agent_test: Always report AUROC or resolution beside ECE; do not use stated confidence alone as the abstain trigger
